description:
## Goal

Implement the `defevent` macro. It generates a typed event module with a struct,
`@type t`, `encode/1` (struct → JSON binary), `decode/1` (JSON binary or map →
struct), and compile-time validation of field declarations.

This is a standalone Elixir macro with no runtime dependency on other Filament
modules. It can be developed and tested independently.

## Deviation policy

Any deviation from this spec requires prior approval. Stop work, run
`bw comment <ticket-id> "..."` describing the conflict, reopen the ticket, and await
guidance. Do not improvise.

---

## 1. Filament.Event module (macro host)

FILE: lib/filament/event.ex

```elixir
defmodule Filament.Event do
  @moduledoc """
  Macro for defining typed event structs with JSON encode/decode.

  Usage (inside any module or at top-level):

      import Filament.Event

      defevent CartAdded do
        field :product_id, :string, required: true
        field :quantity,   :integer, default: 1
        field :note,       :string                  # optional, no default
      end

  This creates the module CartAdded (namespaced under the calling module)
  with a struct, @type t, encode/1, and decode/1.

  If called from MyApp.Cart, the generated module is MyApp.Cart.CartAdded.
  If called at the top level of a module, it is namespaced under that module.
  """

  @supported_types [:string, :integer, :float, :boolean, :atom]
  @valid_field_opts [:required, :default]

  defmacro defevent(name, do: block) do
    caller_module = __CALLER__.module
    event_module = Module.concat(caller_module, name)

    # Parse field declarations from the block
    fields = extract_fields(block, __CALLER__)

    # Validate at compile time
    Enum.each(fields, fn field -> validate_field!(field, __CALLER__) end)

    # Build struct fields list: required fields have no default (enforced via @enforce_keys)
    # optional fields with :default get their default value
    # optional fields without :default default to nil
    enforce_keys =
      fields
      |> Enum.filter(& &1.required)
      |> Enum.map(& &1.name)

    struct_fields =
      Enum.map(fields, fn
        %{name: n, default: d} when d != :__no_default__ -> {n, d}
        %{name: n} -> {n, nil}
      end)

    type_fields =
      Enum.map(fields, fn %{name: n, type: t} ->
        {n, elixir_type_ast(t)}
      end)

    quote do
      defmodule unquote(event_module) do
        @enforce_keys unquote(enforce_keys)
        defstruct unquote(struct_fields)

        @type t :: %__MODULE__{unquote_splicing(type_fields)}

        @doc "Encode this event to a JSON binary."
        @spec encode(t()) :: {:ok, binary()} | {:error, term()}
        def encode(%__MODULE__{} = event) do
          Jason.encode(Map.from_struct(event))
        end

        @doc "Decode a JSON binary or string-keyed map into this event struct."
        @spec decode(binary() | map()) :: {:ok, t()} | {:error, term()}
        def decode(data) when is_binary(data) do
          case Jason.decode(data) do
            {:ok, map} -> decode(map)
            {:error, _} = err -> err
          end
        end

        def decode(map) when is_map(map) do
          fields = unquote(Macro.escape(fields))
          enforce = unquote(enforce_keys)

          result =
            Enum.reduce_while(fields, {:ok, %{}}, fn field, {:ok, acc} ->
              key_str = Atom.to_string(field.name)

              case Map.fetch(map, key_str) do
                {:ok, value} ->
                  case cast_field(value, field.type) do
                    {:ok, cast} -> {:cont, {:ok, Map.put(acc, field.name, cast)}}
                    {:error, _} = err -> {:halt, err}
                  end

                :error when field.required ->
                  {:halt, {:error, {:missing_field, field.name}}}

                :error ->
                  default = if field.default == :__no_default__, do: nil, else: field.default
                  {:cont, {:ok, Map.put(acc, field.name, default)}}
              end
            end)

          case result do
            {:ok, attrs} -> {:ok, struct!(__MODULE__, attrs)}
            {:error, _} = err -> err
          end
        end

        # ── Private casting ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
        defp cast_field(v, :string) when is_binary(v), do: {:ok, v}
        defp cast_field(v, :integer) when is_integer(v), do: {:ok, v}
        defp cast_field(v, :float) when is_float(v), do: {:ok, v}
        defp cast_field(v, :float) when is_integer(v), do: {:ok, v * 1.0}
        defp cast_field(v, :boolean) when is_boolean(v), do: {:ok, v}
        defp cast_field(v, :atom) when is_binary(v), do: {:ok, String.to_existing_atom(v)}
        defp cast_field(v, :atom) when is_atom(v), do: {:ok, v}
        defp cast_field(v, type), do: {:error, {:type_mismatch, expected: type, got: v}}
      end
    end
  end

  # ── Compile-time helpers (not emitted into generated module) ─────────────────

  defp extract_fields({:__block__, _, stmts}, _caller), do: Enum.map(stmts, &parse_field/1)
  defp extract_fields(single_stmt, _caller), do: [parse_field(single_stmt)]

  defp parse_field({:field, _meta, [name, type | rest]}) do
    opts = List.flatten(rest)
    %{
      name: name,
      type: type,
      required: Keyword.get(opts, :required, false),
      default: Keyword.get(opts, :default, :__no_default__)
    }
  end

  defp validate_field!(%{name: name, type: type, required: req, default: def_}, caller) do
    supported = unquote(@supported_types)
    valid_opts = unquote(@valid_field_opts)

    unless type in supported do
      raise CompileError,
        file: caller.file,
        line: caller.line,
        description:
          "defevent field #{inspect(name)}: unsupported type #{inspect(type)}. " <>
            "Supported: #{inspect(supported)}"
    end

    if req and def_ != :__no_default__ do
      raise CompileError,
        file: caller.file,
        line: caller.line,
        description:
          "defevent field #{inspect(name)}: :required and :default are mutually exclusive"
    end
  end

  defp elixir_type_ast(:string), do: quote(do: String.t())
  defp elixir_type_ast(:integer), do: quote(do: integer())
  defp elixir_type_ast(:float), do: quote(do: float())
  defp elixir_type_ast(:boolean), do: quote(do: boolean())
  defp elixir_type_ast(:atom), do: quote(do: atom())
end
```

IMPORTANT implementation note: The `validate_field!` function uses `unquote/1` inside a
`defp` that is itself inside a `defmacro`. This means `@supported_types` and `@valid_field_opts`
module attributes are evaluated at macro-definition time, not at call site. If that causes
issues, inline the lists as literals instead of unquoting module attributes. If any part of
the macro structure causes compilation errors, stop and comment on the ticket — do not
invent a different macro architecture.

The `cast_field/2` function uses `String.to_existing_atom/1` for `:atom` type. This is
intentional — it prevents atom table exhaustion from untrusted input. If a caller needs
to decode arbitrary atom strings, that is out of scope and requires a separate approach.

## 2. Jason dependency

FILE: filament/mix.exs

`Jason` must be listed as a dependency. Check whether it is already present
(LiveView depends on it transitively). If not present as a direct dep, add:

```elixir
{:jason, "~> 1.4"}
```

Do not add it if it is already a transitive dependency — `mix deps` will confirm.

---

## 3. Tests

FILE: test/filament/event_test.exs

```elixir
defmodule Filament.EventTest do
  use ExUnit.Case, async: true
  import Filament.Event

  defevent TestPurchased do
    field :item_id, :string, required: true
    field :quantity, :integer, default: 1
    field :note, :string
  end

  # Tests below use the generated TestPurchased module.
end
```

Test cases:
1. **struct enforcement** — `%TestPurchased{}` without :item_id raises ArgumentError
2. **default applied** — `%TestPurchased{item_id: "x"}` has quantity: 1 and note: nil
3. **encode round-trip** — encode then decode returns {:ok, original_struct}
4. **decode from string** — JSON string `{"item_id":"abc","quantity":2}` → {:ok, %TestPurchased{...}}
5. **decode missing required** — `{"quantity": 1}` (no item_id) → {:error, {:missing_field, :item_id}}
6. **decode unknown fields ignored** — extra keys in JSON silently dropped
7. **decode type mismatch** — `{"item_id": 123}` (integer where string expected) → {:error, _}
8. **decode optional missing** — `{"item_id": "x"}` with no quantity or note → defaults applied
9. **module namespaced** — `TestPurchased` resolves to `Filament.EventTest.TestPurchased`
10. **compile error: bad type** — `defevent X do field :a, :uuid end` raises CompileError (use assert_raise CompileError in a test that evals the code string)
11. **compile error: required + default** — `defevent X do field :a, :string, required: true, default: "x" end` raises CompileError

Run: `mix test test/filament/event_test.exs`

---

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Filament.Event.defevent` macro compiles and is importable
- [ ] Generated modules have struct, @type t, encode/1, decode/1
- [ ] All 11 test cases pass
- [ ] Dialyzer clean
- [ ] Using an unsupported field type raises CompileError with a useful message
- [ ] Using :required and :default together raises CompileError
